name: Mostly Gone — intro
about: The opening of the Mostly Gone intro. Every date here is the date the MAP holds, not a date written for the script; the renderer re-reads each anchor at run time and aborts if a date in this file disagrees with the page. Playback is deterministic: every value is a pure function of the frame index, nothing is driven by a wall clock, and the same file gives the same frames every time.

music.attribution: Music: Getaway — Benjamin Andrews (YouTube Audio Library)

music.measured: Analysed by geowork/present/analyse_music.py. Near silence at 0 s, up to -20 dBFS by 2 s, building to -10.7 dBFS by 18 s. Swells where the 4 s loudness rises fastest: 6.0, 12.5, 19.5, 30.0, 51.0, 64.0, 92.5 and 101.0 s. A local ease at 46 s. Autocorrelation of the onset envelope gives 76.0 BPM, which is the dotted/half level of the ~112 BPM the founder measured by ear — the same pulse counted differently, not a disagreement.
music.snapped: Beat boundaries sit on measured onsets: 5.76, 18.92, 29.98 (the strongest hit in the first 110 s, strength 0.961), 39.96, 52.60, 64.96, 77.86, 92.06. The full-trail reveal opens on 92.06 so the 92.5 s swell carries it.

trail.pace: PRESENTATIONAL, NOT A DATED CLAIM. The trail grows on this file's narrative clock so a viewer can follow it to the show. The routes it is joined from span 250,000 to 13,000 years ago, are not contemporaneous with each other, and are not tied to the date on the slider.
trail.geometry: Joined from the map's own ROUTES by geowork/present/build_trail.py. Americas: r01 + r03 (to the vertex it shares with r05) + r05, no gaps. Anatolia: r92 + r97 (to its last vertex heading into southeast Turkey), no gaps. The final 276 km from there to Göbekli Tepe has NO route on this map and is not drawn.

beat_order_note: The beats run in DATE order, as ruled, which is not the order the brief listed them in. The map dates Monte Verde to 14,500 ya and the Sahara's Holocene onset to 14,800 ya, so the Sahara comes first. Arabia's only post-glacial wet window opens at 10,500 ya, later than Göbekli Tepe at 11,526, so Arabia follows the Göbekli landing. The clock never runs backwards.

shots.card:
Eleven thousand six hundred years ago, someone built this.
They had no farms, no writing, no metal.
EDITOR’S GAP — Göbekli Tepe pillar footage or stills go here. Deliberately left empty: no image of unknown licence has been pulled into this render.

shots.line: To understand who, you have to see the world they walked out of.
The ice begins to let go of North America.
A corridor opens between the two ice sheets.
The rains return to the Sahara, and its rivers fill.
And possibly already at the far end of the Americas.

shots.deserts_note: Deserts are NOT listed for this beat. At this camera the field is stretched past its own 0.1 degree cells and reads as soft ovals over Syria and Iraq, so presentation mode fades it out across zoom 4-5. Leaving it in the layer list would put a row in the legend for something not on screen.

shots.line: It wasn’t one site. It was a network.
shots.note: Sayburç is the only one of the four Taş Tepeler anchors on the map. Karahan Tepe, Çakmaktepe and Nevalı Çori are held: their cited publications give no coordinates, the PPND database is erroring, and the official project pages carry no coordinate list. Founder-ruled 2026-10-28: ship Sayburç, hold the rest. None was invented.

shots.contact_note: MEASURED AT THIS CAMERA, NOT SUPPOSED. The whole 299 km corridor is 77 px long here, so the dash is a fraction of the drawn length (period 3.85 px, about twenty stitches) rather than a fixed [1,9], which would have given eight dots. The open rings at the digs need about 22 px of path each and do NOT draw at 77 px: six of them would overlap into one cyan clump. 111 px of cyan ink in a 38x43 box, fill ratio 0.068 -- a thread, not a blob.

The contact link is COMPLETE on this beat and still drawn, but it is NOT in the layer list and so has no legend row. At this camera (zoom 2) the corridor measures 6 px end to end and leaves 8 pixels of ink. The 276 km gap it closes is 9 px at the same scale, so neither the gap nor the link is resolvable here. A legend row for eight pixels is advertising, which is the fault the desert fade was built to remove. The beat where this link can actually be read is `network`.

contact.claim: CONTACT, NOT MIGRATION. Six excavated Pre-Pottery Neolithic sites between the northern Levant and the Urfa plateau -- Tell Qaramel, Mureybet, Jerf el Ahmar, Tell Halula, Nevali Cori, Gobekli Tepe -- joined to say that these places were in contact with one another. It does NOT say a population walked the line.
contact.why_separate: The amber trail is built from ROUTES, which on this map assert that people walked. Asouti 2006 (Journal of World Prehistory) argues the PPNB interaction sphere and its diffusion model are too abstractly defined to support that reading here, and that the site distribution is very equivocal about the cultural prominence of any particular area. So the link is drawn thinner, fainter and differently dashed, in a colour the trail never uses, with its own legend row.
contact.pace: It arrives on the network beat. Its progress runs 0 to 1 across that beat's camera move and completes exactly as the camera lands, so the Anatolia branch is seen to reach Gobekli Tepe honestly rather than by an invented route.
